notes: §1985:IX.1.3.5 GR3: "If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement, a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector and that procedure is executed and control is transferred according to the rules of the USE statement. The NOT INVALID KEY phrase is ignored, if specified." The execution arms conform at 85 and have no edition arm (the code is the 2023 rule's): each keyed statement (KeyedIoEmitter EmitWrite, EmitRead, EmitRewrite, EmitDelete, EmitStart) passes invalidKeyHandled = 'the INVALID KEY imperative is present' to EmitUseHook, whose __IoCheck (EmitUseMachinery) runs the file-name or open-mode USE procedure on a '2x' status only when the statement has no INVALID KEY phrase; EmitInvalid/EmitPhrasePair run the INVALID KEY imperative on '2x' only (IoStatusClass.InvalidKey) and the NOT INVALID KEY imperative on '0x' only, so the NOT phrase is ignored after an invalid key and the INVALID KEY phrase is ignored without one. Probed for WRITE, READ, DELETE, REWRITE and START with a USE ... ON I-O procedure: the procedure runs exactly when the phrase is absent. What is missing is the requirement itself, the one point the change record says 1985 has and 2023 dropped: a statement with neither an INVALID KEY phrase nor an associated USE procedure is accepted at --std 85 and the condition passes in silence. kb/Work PB5076 owns that missing check (it lists the statements' own syntax rules, §1985:IX.4.9.3 SR3 and its siblings; this rule id is not in its list). The witness runs a WRITE with only NOT INVALID KEY under a file-name USE procedure.

next.reason: 1985: if INVALID KEY is not specified 'a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector and that procedure is executed'. 2023 drops the requirement: §2023:9.1.14 GR3 runs any applicable exception processing statements (USE declaratives, §2023:9.1.12 GR2) and 'If control is returned from those statements or there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement', and §2023:9.1.14 GR4 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement and there are no applicable exception processing statements' continues the same way. Looser: a program with neither INVALID KEY nor USE is now conforming; EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY is nonfatal, so no refusal became a fatal exception. The paragraph on no invalid key condition is carried verbatim in GR4's trailing text.
